subject: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@veridian.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@veridian.com>, Veridian QA <qa@veridian.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re preparing the internal <500k monthly active user> rollout and need to finalize acceptance criteria so our SREs can schedule an in-house load window. High level asks: latency p95 <= 380ms for 512-token requests, sustained throughput to 300 qps for a 30-minute soak, and warm-cache tail latency checks.

Can you send the Redwood runbook you recommend for the first validation? Also confirm what evidence artifacts you’ll share (per-route telemetry, token cost breakdown, traces). We’re aiming for a test window on Thurs 11/20 between 10:00–13:00 PT.

If possible, loop in whoever owns the telemetry export and the run orchestration so we can align on payload shapes.

Best,
Sam
Sam Park
Head of Engineering
Veridian Health
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@veridian.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling

Sam —

Thanks — this is a great summary and the window works for us. Quick answers and next steps below.

Summary of acceptance targets (we’ll publish these in the runbook):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for 128/256/512 token profiles; p95 for 512-token <= 380ms (target) / 450ms (max).
- Throughput: sustained 300 qps for 30 minutes with <3% error rate.
- Tail: 99.9th percentile of tail requests under cold-start conditions <= 1.2s.
- Quality: brief smoke on 200 random prompts to validate output stability (no major hallucination regressions).

Artifacts we'll provide:
- Redwood benchmark playbook (run steps, traffic scripts) — attachment.
- Telemetry export (per-route token counts, avg/percentile latencies, CPU/GPU utilization) — CSV sample attached.
- Full run log & JSON results post-run.

Ben, Monica — can you confirm who will own the run orchestration and telemetry push to Veridian’s Drive link? Ben: can Redwood supply a short load script (k6 + sample profile) and a small helper to map our route names to Veridian’s test harness? Monica: can CS publish the pass/fail checklist and definition for the quality smoke?

Sam — I’ll upload the playbook and telemetry sample in a minute. I’m tentatively scheduling the Redwood side engineers for the 11/20 10:00–13:00 PT window; if you need a different slot let me know.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@veridian.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling

Looping in Dev for orchestration details. Quick technical notes:
- We’ll run against the dedicated test model instance Veridian is pointed at (please confirm endpoint and key rotation policy).
- Load script: I’ll attach a k6 script parameterized for token sizes and concurrency. It supports a warm-up ramp and a 30-minute steady-state phase.
- Telemetry: we’ll push a CSV with per-second aggregates and a JSON results file with percentiles and per-route failure details.
- Cost telemetry: we can provide a token & GPU-utilization breakdown for the window so Procurement can validate cost against committed usage.

Dev — can you add a small helper that emits trace IDs so Veridian QA can reconcile samples with Redwood traces? Keep it lightweight; a header x-rw-run-id should be fine.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@veridian.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling

Thanks — I’ve posted the k6 script and a small run helper in the shared Drive (link below). Implementation notes:
- k6 profile accepts variables: TARGET_QPS, TOKEN_PROFILE (128|256|512), WARMUP_SECONDS, DURATION_SECONDS.
- Script will add header x-rw-run-id and a unique trace id per request.
- We’ll reserve one numeric model slot for the run and set concurrency to avoid noisier multi-tenant interference.

Attachments included for the Veridian run: redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.pdf, telemetry-schema-sample.csv. Post-run I’ll upload veridian-run-results-20251120.json with full percentiles and raw error counters.

Shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Veridian/Acceptance-Evidence

If QA needs any special payloads (PII-masked templates, long-token prompts), reply-all with examples and I’ll incorporate.

— Dev
Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@veridian.com>, Veridian QA <qa@veridian.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance criteria & load test scheduling — run wrap & evidence

Sam/QA — great run this morning. Summary and evidence links below.

High-level result: PASS (meets target)
- 512-token p95 = 362ms (target 380ms)
- Sustained throughput = 305 qps for 30 minutes, error rate = 1.8% (under 3%)
- Tail: 99.9th = 1.12s
- Quality smoke: 200 prompts, 95% conforming outputs, 5% flagged for manual review (examples in the evidence folder).

Artifacts uploaded to the shared Drive:
- veridian-run-results-20251120.json (complete run metrics and per-route failures)
- telemetry-schema-sample.csv (per-second aggregates)
- redwood-benchmark-playbook-v1.pdf (run steps + pass/fail checklist)
- cost-breakdown-20251120.csv (token counts and estimated GPU minutes)

Next steps we propose:
1) Veridian QA to review the flagged prompts and confirm whether any model tuning is required (deadline: 2025-11-25).
2) Procurement to review cost-breakdown and confirm billing expectations (cc: procure@veridian.com).
3) If accepted, we’ll schedule production cutover run (short smoke + routing) the week of 12/1 — please propose preferred days.

If you want a short readout, Ben and I can do a 30-min handoff with SRE and Procurement tomorrow.

Thanks everyone for quick coordination — filing this evidence to the deal record: https://app.redwood.com/deals/VER-2025-1142

— Lauren
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
